extracted.intended_audience: FCC licensees and permittees, broadcast and wireless station operators, their counsel, and FCC staff handling adjudicatory proceedings and petitions for reconsideration
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules governing Commission-initiated modifications, notices of violations, show-cause and revocation/cease-and-desist hearings, consent orders, and petitions for reconsideration/review under FCC Part 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and protest period for Commission-initiated license/permit modification
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever it appears that a station license or construction permit should be modified, the Commission shall notify the licensee or permittee in writing of the proposed action and reasons and afford the licensee or permittee at least thirty days to protest such proposed order of modification, except that, where safety of life or property is involved, the Commission may by order provide a shorter period of time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification may be effectuated by a notice of proposed rulemaking for FM/TV allotments/assignments. For Wireless Radio Services, Commission shall notify by email and afford at least 30 days; if notification is by Federal Register publication, afford at least 30 days after publication. Exceptions for safety-of-life or property allow shorter periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative protestors' right to protest proposed modification
rubrics_metrics.description: Any other licensee or permittee who believes that its license or permit would be modified by the proposed action may also protest the proposed action before its effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party protests (not just the directly-affected licensee) are permitted; protests must be timely (see notification timing above) and are subject to applicable statutory requirements (e.g., §309 for petitions to deny where relevant).

rubrics_metrics.name: Protests subject to Communications Act §309 requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any protest filed pursuant to this section shall be subject to the requirements of section 309 of the Communications Act of 1934, as amended, for petitions to deny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protests must meet the procedural and substantive requirements set out in §309 where that statutory framework applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proceeding and proof in modification hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: In any case where a hearing proceeding is conducted pursuant to the provisions of this section, both the burden of proceeding with the introduction of evidence and the burden of proof shall be upon the Commission except that, with respect to any issue that pertains to the question of whether the proposed action would modify the license or permit of a person filing a protest pursuant to paragraph (c) of this section, such burdens shall be as described by the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default allocation places both burdens on the Commission; limited exceptions may be specified by the Commission for issues about whether a protestant's license would be modified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing a written appearance to invoke hearing rights
rubrics_metrics.description: To use the right to a hearing and the opportunity to give evidence upon the issues specified in any order designating a matter for hearing, any licensee or permittee, itself or by counsel, shall, within the period of time as may be specified in that order, file with the Commission a written appearance stating that it will present evidence on the matters specified in the order and, if required, appear before the presiding officer at a date and time to be determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The written appearance must affirm intent to present evidence; failure to file the required written appearance may result in waiver of hearing rights (see waiver rules). Timing is as specified in the designation order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of protest or hearing rights and deadline for showing good cause
rubrics_metrics.description: The right to file a protest or the right to a hearing proceeding shall, unless good cause is shown in a petition to be filed not later than 5 days before the lapse of time specified in paragraph (a) or (f) of this section, be deemed waived: (1) In case of failure to timely file the protest or the required written statement; (2) In case of filing a written statement but failing to appear at the hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition showing good cause must be filed at least 5 days before the lapse of the relevant period. Failure to meet timing or to appear results in waiver, which has substantive effects (see effect of waiver).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of waiver of protest/hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the right to file a protest or have a hearing is waived, the licensee or permittee will be deemed to have consented to the modification as proposed and a final decision may be issued by the Commission accordingly. Irrespective of any waiver the Commission may, on its own motion, designate the proposed modification for hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waiver exposes the licensee/permittee to issuance of a final modification order; however the Commission retains discretion to designate for hearing despite waiver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content and service of orders of modification
rubrics_metrics.description: Any order of modification issued pursuant to this section shall include a statement of the findings and the grounds and reasons therefor, shall specify the effective date of the modification, and shall be served on the licensee or permittee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Orders must state findings and grounds and give an effective date; service on affected parties is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predesignation pleading procedure for broadcast investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: In cases where an investigation is being conducted in connection with the operation of a broadcast station or a pending renewal application, the licensee may file a written statement setting forth its views regarding the matters under investigation; staff may in its discretion advise the licensee of the general nature of the investigation and its opportunity to submit such a statement. Any filing by the licensee will be forwarded to the Commission with any staff memorandum recommending action. Ex parte rules continue to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Predesignation statements are a way for licensees to present views prior to designation; staff discretion governs advisories; ex parte rules (e.g., §1.1203) are not superseded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of violations — notice before revocation/suspension except particular cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Except in cases of willfulness or those in which public health, interest, or safety requires otherwise, any person who holds a license, permit or other authorization appearing to have violated any provision will, before revocation, suspension, or cease and desist proceedings are instituted, be served with a written notice calling these facts to his or her attention and requesting a statement concerning the matter. FCC Form 793 may be used. The Notice of Violation may be combined with a Notice of Apparent Liability; in that event §1.80 applies and not §1.89.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice requirement is the default prior-to-enforcement step except for willfulness/safety exceptions. Combining notices triggers different procedural code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response timing and method to Notice of Violation
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 10 days from receipt of notice or such other period as may be specified, the recipient shall send a written answer, in duplicate, directly to the Commission office originating the official notice. If an answer cannot be sent within such 10-day period by reason of illness or other unavoidable circumstance, acknowledgment and answer shall be made at the earliest practicable date with a satisfactory explanation of the delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default answer deadline is 10 days (unless another period specified). Answers should be sent in duplicate to the originating office; illness or unavoidable circumstances require prompt acknowledgment and explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of answer to Notice of Violation
rubrics_metrics.description: The answer shall be complete in itself and shall not be abbreviated by reference to other communications. The answer shall contain a statement of action taken to correct the condition or omission complained of and to preclude its recurrence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replies must be self-contained and include corrective measures and preventive steps. Additional required information depends on the nature of the violation (see apparatus/operator specifics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific information required when violations relate to transmitting apparatus
rubrics_metrics.description: If the notice relates to violations that may be due to the physical or electrical characteristics of transmitting apparatus and any new apparatus is to be installed, the answer shall state the date such apparatus was ordered, the name of the manufacturer, and the promised date of delivery. If installation requires a construction permit, the file number shall be given, or if none assigned, identification sufficient for ready identification of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide procurement and application identifiers to demonstrate corrective action timeline and intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific information required when violations relate to transmitter operation
rubrics_metrics.description: If the notice relates to lack of attention to or improper operation of the transmitter, the name and license number of the operator in charge (where applicable) shall be given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify responsible personnel and their license numbers when operation is at issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order to show cause for revocation/cease-and-desist and hearing designation
rubrics_metrics.description: If it appears a station license or construction permit should be revoked and/or a cease and desist order issued, the Commission will issue an order directing the person to show cause why such an order should not be issued. The order will designate for hearing the matters inquired and call upon the respondent to file a written appearance stating it will present evidence and, if required, appear before a presiding officer, but no earlier than thirty days after receipt (shorter if safety involved).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show-cause orders initiate adjudication; they specify hearing matters and set timelines (typically minimum 30 days to respond unless safety exception).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural deadlines to file written appearance in show-cause proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondents shall, personally or by counsel, file with the Commission, within twenty days of the mailing of the order or such shorter period as may be specified therein, a written appearance stating they will present evidence and, if required, appear before the presiding officer. The presiding officer may accept a late-filed appearance for good cause shown, but a late appearance requires a petition stating particular facts/reasons and will be granted only if the presiding officer determines good cause exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is a twenty-day filing rule (subject to order-specified shorter period); late filings require a particularized petition demonstrating good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof in revocation/cease-and-desist hearings and potential expedition
rubrics_metrics.description: In all such revocation and/or cease and desist hearings, the burden of proceeding with and of proof shall be upon the Commission; the Commission may specify in a show cause order, when circumstances require expedition, shortened times for initial decision effectiveness, filing exceptions, requests for oral argument, and notices of intention to participate in oral argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission typically bears burdens; it can also impose expedited procedural deadlines in the show-cause order where warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of corrections/promises to correct in revocation proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Correction of or promise to correct the conditions complained of in a show cause order shall not preclude issuance of a cease and desist order, but corrections or promises and the past record may be considered in determining whether revocation and/or a cease and desist order should be issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remedial steps are relevant to mitigation but do not automatically prevent enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content and service of orders after revocation hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Any order of revocation and/or cease and desist order issued after hearing shall include a statement of findings and the grounds therefor, shall specify the effective date of the order, and shall be served on the person to whom such order is directed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjudicatory final orders must contain findings, grounds, effective date, and must be served on the respondent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Events constituting waiver of hearing after order to show cause
rubrics_metrics.description: After issuance of an order to show cause, the occurrence of any one of: (1) respondent fails to file a timely written appearance as prescribed; (2) respondent, having filed timely appearance, fails to present evidence or appear; (3) respondent files timely written statement expressly waiving rights to a hearing — will constitute a waiver of such hearing and the proceeding thereafter will be conducted under the after-waiver provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waiver is triggered by failure to comply with appearance/presentation requirements or by an express waiver in writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission and consideration of written statement when hearing waived
rubrics_metrics.description: When a hearing is waived under specified provisions, a written statement signed by the respondent denying or seeking to mitigate/justify the circumstances may be submitted within the time specified for a written appearance. The Commission in its discretion may accept a late statement; late statements require a petition showing particularized facts/reasons and good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After waiver, respondents may still submit written mitigation; late submissions need a supporting petition demonstrating good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presiding officer action and certification when hearing is waived
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever a hearing is waived the presiding officer shall, at the earliest practicable date, issue an order reciting the events or circumstances constituting waiver and terminating the hearing proceeding. A presiding officer other than the Commission shall also certify the case to the Commission. Such order shall be served upon the respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural closure requires a recitation of waiver events, termination, certification if appropriate, and service on respondent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and scope of a 'consent order'
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'consent order' is a formal decree accepting an agreement between a party to an adjudicatory hearing proceeding (held to determine whether that party has violated statutes or Commission rules or policies) and the appropriate operating Bureau, securing future compliance and disposing of all issues on which the proceeding was designated for hearing. The order is issued by the officer designated to preside at the hearing proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consent orders resolve designated hearing issues by agreement and secure future compliance; they are formal decrees signed by the presiding officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on matters subject to negotiation for consent orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Consent orders may not be negotiated with respect to matters which involve a party's basic statutory qualifications to hold a license (see 47 U.S.C. 308 and 309).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agreements cannot be used to settle issues that go to the basic statutory qualifications for licensure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiation and timing of consent order negotiations
rubrics_metrics.description: Negotiations leading to a consent order may be initiated by the operating Bureau or by a party whose possible violations are issues in the proceeding, at any time after designation for hearing. The presiding officer shall be notified; parties should be prepared at the initial prehearing conference to state willingness to enter negotiations. If unwilling, the hearing proceeds; if willing, parties will be afforded opportunity to negotiate before the hearing is commenced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Negotiations can begin post-designation; parties must notify the presiding officer and may seek a pause or abeyance of the hearing while negotiating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation rights of other parties in consent negotiations
rubrics_metrics.description: Other parties to the proceeding are entitled, but are not required, to participate in the negotiations, and may join in any agreement which is reached.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third parties may choose to participate in settlement talks and may opt into agreements reached.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required elements of every consent agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Every agreement shall contain: (1) an admission of all jurisdictional facts; (2) a waiver of the usual procedures for preparation and review of an initial decision; (3) a waiver of the right of judicial review or otherwise to challenge the validity of the consent order; (4) a statement that the designation order may be used in construing the consent order; (5) a statement that the agreement shall become part of the record only if the consent order is signed by the presiding officer and the time for review has passed without rejection by the Commission; (6) a statement that the agreement is for purposes of settlement only and that its signing does not constitute an admission by any party of any violation of law, rules or policy; and (7) a draft order for signature of the presiding officer resolving by consent, and for the future, all issues specified in the designation order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agreements must include each listed element exactly to be eligible for submission as a consent order; inclusion of the draft order is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presiding officer options after submission of a consent agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: If agreement is reached it shall be submitted to the presiding officer, who shall either sign the order, reject the agreement, or suggest to the parties that negotiations continue on unsatisfactory portions. If signed, the record shall be closed. If rejected, the hearing continues. If further negotiations are suggested and parties agree to resume negotiating, the presiding officer may decide whether to hold the hearing in abeyance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presiding officer has discretion to accept, reject, or request further negotiation; acceptance closes the record; rejection continues the hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal and Commission review of consent orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party who has not joined in any agreement which is reached may appeal the consent order under §1.302, and the Commission may review the agreement on its own motion. If the Commission rejects the consent order, the proceeding will be remanded for further proceedings. If the Commission does not reject it, it shall be entered in the record as a final order and is subject to judicial review only by parties who did not join in the agreement. The Commission may revise the agreement and consent order; private parties may accept the revision or withdraw. If a party withdraws from a revision, the consent order will not be issued and the proceeding remanded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-consenting parties retain appeal rights; the Commission has supervisory authority to accept, reject, or revise consent orders; revisions may prompt withdrawal and remand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and availability of negotiating papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Negotiating papers constitute work product, are available to parties participating in negotiations, but are not routinely available for public inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement negotiation materials are protected from routine public disclosure but are shared among negotiating parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions and issues in proceedings alleging violation of a consent order
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation of a consent order shall subject the consenting party to any and all sanctions which could have been imposed in the proceeding resulting in the consent order if all issues had been decided against the consenting party and to any further sanctions agreed upon in the consent order. The Commission shall have the burden of showing that the consent order has been violated in some (but not in every) respect. Violation and sanctions shall be the only issues considered in such a proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceedings on alleged consent-order violations are narrowly focused on whether a violation occurred and what sanctions are appropriate; Commission bears burden of proof of violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective dates of final actions following review of an initial decision (delegated authority)
rubrics_metrics.description: Final decisions of a commissioner, or panel of commissioners following review of an initial decision shall be effective 40 days after public release of the full text of such final decision. If a petition for reconsideration of such final decision is filed, the effect of the decision is stayed until 40 days after release of the final order disposing of the petition. If an application for review is filed or the Commission orders the record for review, the effect is stayed until the Commission's review is completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard 40-day effective date and stays apply to final decisions following review; petitions and applications for review can cause stays as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective dates for non-hearing and interlocutory actions under delegated authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-hearing or interlocutory actions taken pursuant to delegated authority shall, unless otherwise ordered by the designated authority, be effective upon release of the document containing the full text of such action, or if no full-text document is released, upon release of a public notice announcing the action. The designated authority may in its discretion stay effect of a non-hearing action pending disposition of a petition for reconsideration. Petitions for reconsideration of interlocutory actions will not be entertained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-hearing actions usually take effect on release; designated authorities can stay effect for reconsideration; interlocutory actions are not subject to petitions for reconsideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default effective date of Commission actions and finality date for review
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise specified by law or Commission rule, the effective date of any Commission action shall be the date of public notice of such action. The Commission may designate an earlier or later effective date, which has no effect on pleading periods. Commission action shall be deemed final, for purposes of seeking reconsideration at the Commission or judicial review, on the date of public notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public notice date is both default effective date and the date that triggers rights to seek reconsideration or judicial review (finality).

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline to preserve right of review — filing petition for reconsideration or application for review
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person desiring Commission consideration of a final action taken pursuant to delegated authority shall file either a petition for reconsideration or an application for review (but not both) within 30 days from the date of public notice of such action. The petition for reconsideration will be acted on by the designated authority or referred to the Commission. A petition for reconsideration of an order designating a matter for hearing will in all cases be referred to the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict 30-day filing rule to preserve review rights; cannot file both petition and application; referential rules for orders designating for hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral practice when parties file both reconsideration and review
rubrics_metrics.description: If one party files a petition for reconsideration and a second party files an application for review, the Commission will withhold action on the application for review until final action has been taken on the petition for reconsideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing by multiple parties triggers suspension of the application's processing pending resolution of reconsideration petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and processing of petitions for reconsideration in non-rulemaking proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions requesting reconsideration of a final Commission action in non-rulemaking proceedings will be acted on by the Commission. Petitions requesting reconsideration of other final actions taken pursuant to delegated authority will be acted on by the designated authority or referred. A petition for reconsideration of an order designating a case for hearing will be entertained only if it relates to an adverse ruling with respect to petitioner's participation. Petitions for reconsideration of other interlocutory actions will not be entertained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines which categories of petition are entertained by Commission vs. designated authority and excludes reconsideration for interlocutory actions (except as stated).

rubrics_metrics.name: Presiding officer certification request procedure on policy question
rubrics_metrics.description: Within the period allowed for filing a petition for reconsideration, any party to the proceeding may request the presiding officer to certify to the Commission the question as to whether, on policy in effect at the time of designation or adopted since designation, and undisputed facts, a hearing should be held. If the presiding officer finds substantial doubt he will certify the policy question to the Commission. No appeal may be filed from an order denying such a request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties can seek certification of threshold policy questions; presiding officer's certification decision is final and not appealable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file a petition for reconsideration and required showing for non-parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party to the proceeding, or any other person whose interests are adversely affected by any action taken by the Commission or designated authority, may file a petition requesting reconsideration. If filed by a non-party, it must state with particularity how the person's interests are adversely affected and show good reason why they could not participate earlier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-parties bear the burden to show how they are adversely affected and why they didn't participate previously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible grounds for petitions filed after denial of application for review
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Commission has denied an application for review, a petition for reconsideration will be entertained only if: (i) it relies on facts or arguments which relate to events/circumstances occurring/changed since last opportunity; or (ii) it relies on facts or arguments unknown to petitioner until after last opportunity and which could not, with ordinary diligence, have been learned earlier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-denial petitions must present newly arisen or newly discovered facts/arguments meeting the specified standards; otherwise may be dismissed as repetitious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specificity requirement for petitions and relief requested
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for reconsideration shall state with particularity the respects in which petitioner believes the action should be changed and shall state specifically the form of relief sought; it may contain alternative requests. If the decision sets forth formal findings and conclusions, the petition shall cite the findings/conclusions believed erroneous and state with particularity how they should be changed; may request additional findings/conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions must be particularized and state precise relief; general or vague claims are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electrical interference affidavit requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a petition for reconsideration is based upon a claim of electrical interference to an existing station or a station with a construction permit, such petition must be accompanied by an affidavit of a qualified radio engineer showing that electrical interference will be caused within the station's normally protected contour, by following prescribed procedures or measurements in the chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical interference claims require a qualified engineer's affidavit with specified showing; failure to include the affidavit is grounds for dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and length limits for petitions, oppositions, and replies
rubrics_metrics.description: Petition for reconsideration and any supplement must be filed within 30 days from public notice of action and shall not exceed 25 double spaced typewritten pages. Oppositions due within 10 days and not exceed 25 pages. Replies due within 7 days after last day for oppositions, not exceed 10 pages and limited to matters raised in the opposition. Supplements filed after 30-day period will not be considered except upon leave granted upon separate pleading stating grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict page limits and filing windows apply; extensions or late supplements require separate leave motions with justifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing format and submission channels for petitions and related pleadings
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions, oppositions, and replies shall conform to §§1.49, 1.51, 1.52 and, except for licensing matters in the Wireless Radio Service (para (o)), shall be submitted to the Secretary by mail, commercial courier, hand, or electronic submission through the Commission's Electronic Comment Filing System or other electronic filing system. Petitions submitted only by electronic mail or directly to staff without submission to the Secretary shall not be considered properly filed. Parties filing in electronic form need submit only one copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow specified formatting rules and required filing channels; omission of required filing method (e.g., only email) renders filing improper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition and timing of Commission action on petitions for reconsideration
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission or designated authority may grant the petition in whole or part or may deny or dismiss it. Its order will contain a concise statement of reasons. Where petition relates to an instrument of authorization granted without hearing, the Commission or designated authority will take such action within 90 days after the petition is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission issues a reasoned order on petitions; 90-day target applies to petitions contesting authorizations granted without hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies available when petition for reconsideration is granted
rubrics_metrics.description: If granted the Commission or designated authority may: (i) simultaneously reverse or modify the order from which reconsideration is sought; (ii) remand the matter to a bureau or personnel for further proceedings including rehearing; or (iii) order other appropriate proceedings. If further proceedings are initiated, ruling on the merits is deferred pending their completion; after completion, Commission may affirm, reverse, modify or remand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relief can include reversal, modification, remand, or ordering additional proceedings; effect depends on subsequent proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on new evidence on rehearing
rubrics_metrics.description: No evidence other than newly discovered evidence, evidence which has become available only since the original taking of evidence, or evidence which the Commission or designated authority believes should have been taken in the original proceeding shall be taken on any rehearing ordered pursuant to this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rehearings are limited to new or newly available evidence or evidence the Commission believes should have been taken originally; re-litigation via re-introduction of old evidence is not permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of filing a petition for reconsideration on judicial review and compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing a petition for reconsideration is not a condition precedent to judicial review of any action except where the person seeking review was not a party to the proceeding or relies on questions of fact or law upon which the Commission was afforded no opportunity to pass. The filing of a petition does not excuse compliance with Commission orders absent special order of the Commission, although upon good cause shown the Commission will stay effectiveness pending decision on the petition (applies only to en banc Commission actions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition for reconsideration generally not required before seeking judicial review; filing a petition does not automatically stay enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing requirement for petitions in Wireless Radio Services
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions for reconsideration of licensing actions, as well as oppositions and replies thereto, filed with respect to the Wireless Radio Services, must be filed electronically via ULS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wireless Radio Service contest filings have a mandatory electronic-only channel (ULS); follow service-specific electronic filing requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of petitions plainly not warranting Commission consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions that plainly do not warrant consideration may be dismissed or denied by relevant bureaus/offices. Examples include petitions that: (1) fail to identify any material error, omission, or reason warranting reconsideration; (2) rely on facts/arguments not previously presented and do not meet requirements for new matters; (3) rely on arguments fully considered and rejected by the Commission within the same proceeding; (4) fail to state with particularity required by paragraph (d); (5) relate to matters outside the scope of the order for which reconsideration is sought; (6) omit information required by rules (e.g., engineering affidavit); (7) fail to comply with procedural requirements; (8) relate to an order previously denied on similar grounds (except narrow exceptions); (9) are untimely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The list is illustrative (non-exhaustive) and shows common procedural and substantive defects that justify dismissal without full Commission consideration.
